p: the whole multitude of them arose: Christ, who is now ready to suffer for the rebellion which we raised in this world, is first of all pronounced guiltless, so that it might appear that he suffered not for his own sins (which were none) but for ours.
perverting the nation: Corrupting the people, and leading them into errors.
When Pilate heard of Galilee: Christ is a laughing stock to princes, but to their great pain.

Herod's jurisdiction: This was Herod Antipas the Tetrarch, in the time of whose period of rule (which was almost twenty-two years long) John the Baptist preached and was put to death, and Jesus Christ also died and rose again, and the apostles began to preach, and various things were done at Jerusalem almost seven years after Christ's death. This Herod was sent into banishment to Lyons, about the second year of Gaius Caesar.
men of war set him at: Accompanied with his nobles and soldiers who followed him from Galilee.
And the same day Pilate and: The hatred of godliness binds the wicked together.
And Pilate: Christ is acquitted the second time, even by him of whom he is condemned, so that it might appear in what way he who is just, redeemed us who were unjust.
rulers and the people: Those whom the Jews called the sanhedrin.
I will therefore chastise him: The wisdom of the flesh is to choose the lesser of two evils, but God curses such plans.
And he said unto them the: Christ is acquitted the third time before he is condemned, so that it might appear that it was for our sins that were condemned in him.
And as they led him away: An example of the outrageousness and disorder of the soldiers.
And there followed him a great: The triumph of the wicked has a most horrible end.

green tree: As if he said, "If they do this to me who is always fruitful and flourishing, and who lives forever by reason of my Godhead, what will they do to you who are unfruitful and void of all active righteousness?"
And when they were come to: Christ became accursed for us upon the cross, suffering the punishment which the ones who would belong to God deserved.
Then said Jesus: Christ, in praying for his enemies, shows that he is both the Sacrifice and the Priest.
chosen of God: Whom God loves more than all others.
And a superscription also was written: Pilate is unknowingly made a preacher of the kingdom of Christ.

And: Therefore we must either take Matthew's account to be using the figure of speech synecdoche, or that both of them mocked Christ. But one of them who was eventually overcome with the great patience of God breaks forth in that confession worthy all memory.

one of the malefactors which were: Christ, in the midst of the humbling of himself upon the cross, indeed shows that he has both the power of life to save the believers and the power of death to avenge the rebellious.
amiss: More than he ought.

paradise: God made the visible paradise in the eastern part of the world: but that which we behold with the eyes of our mind is the place of everlasting joy and salvation, through the goodness and mercy of God, a most pleasant rest for the souls of the godly, and a most quiet and joyful dwelling.
And it was about the sixth: Christ, even being at the point of death, shows himself to be God almighty even to the blind.
And the sun was darkened: Christ enters bravely and resolutely into the very darkness of death, and he does this so that he might overcome death even within its most secret places.
Now when the centurion saw what: Christ, as often as it pleases him, causes his very enemies to give honourable witness that he is right.
And all his acquaintance: Christ gathers together and defends his little flock in the midst of the tormentors.
And: Christ, through his well known burial, confirms both the truth of his death as well as his resurrection, by the plain and evident witness of Pilate.

drew on: Literally, "dawning", and now beginning, for the light of the former day drew toward the going down of the sun, and that was the day of preparation for the feast, that is, the feast which was to be kept the following day.

And the women also: Christ, being set upon by the devil and all his instruments, and being even in death's mouth, places weak women in his service, bearing in mind to immediately triumph over these terrible enemies, and that without any great endeavour.
